GENERAL THETA FOUNDATIONS I:
CURRENT TECHNICAL SUPPLEMENT
QIAN QI
Abstract. This is the current technical supplement to General Theta Foundations I. It contains
the complete inherited positive-realization, contrast, nonabelian multiplicity, mean–contrast, spectral
and arithmetic theory, the return-polytope approximation and sharp physical-dictionary law, and
all independent causal, minimax, dual, finite-order measurement, two-stage reset, communication,
discrimination and geometric results. The main article proves the shared-preparation, tied-action
reset-memory and unrestricted-decoder certificates. The statements retained here keep their individ-
ual hypotheses and full proof bodies. Cross-document references and the theorem map identify their
actual logical roles; historical preservation is not an additional mathematical premise.
References to the main article use ordinary section numbers; statements numbered S belong to this
supplement. Native paired compilation resolves references in both directions. The first sections
supply the exact group and Fourier premises used by the shared-device theorems. The inherited
return geometry supplies the upper counterpart to the unrestricted-decoder lower. Subsequent
sections retain the complete independent developments. Relocation does not change a statement’s
hypotheses or priority; two explicit output-visible-core clarifications from the parallel author branch
are identified in the source-provenance and proof-audit records.
S1. A permutation normal form with an exact memory charge
Theorem 3.1 identifies when finite memory exists. We now determine the form of every possible
finite realization, retaining the cost of its prescribed pure initial label. The distinction between
a minimal linear representation and a positive realization remains essential. In particular, the
permutation representation carried by the observable space does not by itself provide a decoder
with values in the probability simplex.
Let b be a compactly reversible response admitting a finite realization. WriteG for its finite
observable group,d = dimVb, andN for its residual cardinality. We use the chronological convention
g(u)g(v) = g(uv): the right action onVb is f·g(w) = Lwf, whereLwf(z) = f(wz). Thus G in
this notation is the opposite of the group of operators with the usual convention for composition;
inversion identifies the two groups. No group cardinality, faithfulness, or representation-theoretic
statement depends on this convention. Every element has a representative inA∗, including its
inverse, since a finite group generated by the command elements is already generated by their
positive words. The valueb(g) =b(w) is consequently well defined.
A probability factorization on a finiteG-set consists of a finite setX, row permutation matrices
Pg withPgPh =Pgh, a probability rowλonX, and a row-stochastic matrixD with columns indexed
byC, such that
b(g) =λPgD (g∈G). (S1.1)
All rows ofD are probability laws, including rows associated with states that are not distinguished
by the immediate terminal measurement. Unused orbits may be deleted. Define
κG(b) = min{|X|: (S1.1) holds}.

GENERAL THETA FOUNDATIONS I:
ACQUIRED GEOMETRY AND CAUSAL RESOURCE TRANSFER
QIAN QI
Abstract. We study finite-resource prediction in positive prepared causal experiments using
an actually prepared comparison law that need not belong to the operating model family. A
reference-side converse replaces only each productive report–audit row while retaining the actual
pre-call occupation. The resulting positive submeasure has controlled missing mass, a cost-certified
density cap and controlled task moments, giving a lower bound uniform over all legal strategies.
A common parameter-independent approximate balancing program gives a matching upper at the
same expected physical budget. The bounds recover exact stopped risk profiles at zero error and
matching acquired-geometry orders on a quantified two-sided calibration regime. Drift certificates
extend the converse to metastable and singular calibration with explicit preparation mass and
residence time. Classical controlled channels and noncommuting quantum instruments verify the
same theorem without an exactly fair operating reference or a posterior-rank floor. A same-task
extension combines attained calibration and causal erasure error. Event-stopped observers may
reuse live labels for outputs, whereas intrinsically state-stopped observers pay for disjoint live and
terminal roles; both resource laws are proved. We retain nonintervening Gaussian sensing with a
joint waiting–output geometry. Numerical precision, program description, workspace, physical time
and simulator states are accounted for separately.
1. Introduction
A prepared causal experiment determines which future tests can be predicted from its reports.
The predictive quotient records this equivalence of executable tests, but does not by itself determine
the geometry that a finite observer can acquire. Waiting for a rare informative report changes both
the attainable law and the physical cost. Persistent memory constrains the route to that report as
well as its final description. A further difficulty is calibration: a comparison law may describe a
physically prepared ideal experiment accurately without being an exact member of the operating
model family. A converse that silently treats it as an admitted model is then unjustified.
We establish a two-sided resource–risk transfer under explicit raw experiment certificates. One
actual witness bounds the effort of every competing strategy and the accumulated discrepancy
of its productive report–audit rows from a prepared comparison law. Separately, one parameter-
independent acquisition program approximately balances the report and task measures in every
operating model. Our center is Theorem 4.1. It uses neither an exact comparison model in the
uncertainty family nor a comparison execution that stops under the competing program.
The main construction in the converse is an accepted comparison submeasure. Retain the actual
distribution of each pre-call history, but replace its current productive report–audit row only. The
resulting positive measure has a controlled mass defect and a density cap set by actual expected
acquisition count. It need not be an executable terminal law. Its unnormalized task moments
nevertheless give an all-strategy risk lower. This separates a valid local comparison from the generally
invalid replacement of an entire selected path law.
Date: October 2026.
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification.Primary 60G40, 62C20; Secondary 28A80, 60J05, 81P15, 94A29.
Key words and phrases.causal experiment, predictive quotient, acquired law, stopped prediction, finite memory,
moment balancing, singular acquisition.

2 QIAN QI

law ν, audit meanf, and residual variancew; its capb retains actual preparation mass. In the
matched-effort, identity-export case the central bounds take the form

defect bounds are actual accumulated charges, not a best-policy occupation estimate. Different
effort constants and export multiplicities remain explicitly distinct in the theorem. The formula
recovers exact equalities at zero errors and matching geometric orders on a quantitative two-sided
calibration regime.
The output width depends on the physical stopping convention. A state-stopped observer has
a state-only halt map; its live and terminal labels are disjoint, giving widthM−B when B live
labels are mandatory and sufficient. An event-stopped observer emits its final commitment during a
transition and may reuse live labels as final outputs, giving widthM. We retain both exact resource
laws and their proof, rather than excluding reuse silently. All intercall phases, clocks and continuing
random seeds are charged.
Theorem 5.2 replaces small uniform defects by a drift certificate on actual good/bad mode
occupation. The initial bad mass and its residence time appear explicitly; singular and changing-
rank report kernels are permitted. Theorems 6.1 and 6.2 verify the same central theorem from a
classical controlled sign channel and a noncommuting positive quantum instrument. Their nominal
balanced preparations need not be operating models. A joint calibration–erasure extension keeps all
errors in the same terminal squared loss, while finite numerical execution and causal simulator costs
are stated separately.
We also retain a different, nonintervening raw application. A current hidden unit vector is observed
through Gaussian noise and is not altered by the observer. Theorem 16.1 proves a matching law

against every legal stopping rule, together with exact finite-output obstructions and a sharp noise
constant. This application is not mislabeled as a post-command balanced task, and its physical
posterior is derived directly from the Gaussian kernel.
The variational profile itself has an established ancestry. Whenw = 0, writinga = 1/b and

retained massa. This is the population trimming formulation underlying trimmedk-means and
impartial trimming [13], [14]. Withw̸= 0 it is the corresponding marked objective. We do not claim
the density cap or low-distortion selection principle as new. Classical reject-option prediction [5], [6],
invariant decision procedures [3], and quantum randomization [4] supply related tools. Approximate
rejection sampling from a fixed independent batch [15], [16] has a different budget and output
objective: here physical attempts can be history dependent, the criterion is an audited decision loss,
and a single finite-state program must work for every admitted model.
Almost-sure expected-cost reachability in partially observed control is studied in [11], and fixed-
memory limit-sure reachability in [12]. Sufficiency results for chattering policies in absorbing decision
processes are developed in [10]. These works concern policy classes and reachability or occupation
criteria; the present matching assertions require, in addition, the specified report–audit balance and
acquisition certificates.
Accumulation of local error along transient occupation and Lyapunov telescoping are standard
stochastic-control techniques. In particular, the occupation-weighted rollout bounds of Hansson
and Wahlberg [17] address policy-specific Bellman approximation and properness. We do not claim
occupation weighting, drift control, or the mere appearance of an expected-time factor as new. Here
the comparison submeasure controls both its lost mass and its task moment against a trimmed

ACQUIRED GEOMETRY AND CAUSAL RESOURCE TRANSFER 3
finite-dictionary optimum, yielding a converse uniform over all admissible observers even when
the comparison process is not an admitted or terminating execution. This combines a different
quantifier structure, a selected geometric objective and explicit stopping-resource widths.
The result is a sufficient-class theorem, not a classification of all positive kernels. Measurable
quotient realization has its separate hypotheses in Appendix A; arbitrary projective arrays are
not declared physical states. Our proofs distinguish new comparison arguments from inherited
exact balance and role counting, and from standard conditional projection, compactness, trimming,
Gaussian tails and covering. Ideal Borel existence is not finite algorithmic synthesis. The certificates
needed to learn unknown kernels, to price every computation optimally, or to treat unbounded
losses and nonterminating protocols are not supplied by the present theorem.
2. Prepared experiments and stopping resources
All state, action and report spaces are standard Borel. An unknown indexθ∈Θ specifies a
prepared law and positive normalized causal kernels (positivity means nonnegative measures, not a
strictly positive density at every report). It is fixed for an entire execution; it may index an arbitrary
history-dependent physical evolution. Policies see only past reports, legal physical commands and
their own allowed coins. They never seeθ. All assertions below are for the declared experiment and
test, not for a formal parameter manifold.
A call has a nonnegative cost bounded below byc∗> 0. A predictable flag declares whether
the call is productive. Commitment is allowed only after a productive report. Conditional on
commitment, a fixed bounded future auditZ∈H is executed, whereH⊂Rk is compact and
convex. This audit is not observed before the prediction is committed. The loss is∥Z−r∥2, r∈H.
Each productive call has a potential audit specified by the same kernel, whether or not the observer
commits there. A fresh stopping coin is independent of that audit conditional on the current physical
report and history. All other informative components of the current report must be included in the
conditional laws below.
The costN in the core theorem counts preparation, failed gate calls, productive calls, and all
calls preceding commitment. A separately required final physical audit has its own explicit cost.
Thus a protocol with one initial preparation call and one final audit uses total raw budgetN + 2,
not N. Time, bit operations and scratch space are not identified with raw-call count.
The stopping interface and retained labels.A checkpoint procedure may retain the entire
precommit history, but its committed value belongs to one fixed dictionary of at mostm elements.
This convention counts only its terminal dictionary, not its full-history working memory. Its physical
acquisition and audit costs are still charged.
A finite-state observer has an alphabetS of at mostM labels and one fixed parameter-independent
program. At every intercall boundary its only observer memory is the retained label. Its next
physical command distribution is a fixed function of that label. In particular, the physical port
identity, elapsed time, prior report and subprogram index are not additional free inputs. During
a call the current command, its report and fresh independent coins are available; the post-report
transition can depend on them. No such coin, report, real register or clock persists unless encoded
in S. A fixed terminal decoderr :S→H reads only the committed label; it never reads the report
or the audit. The two stopping interfaces are as follows.
Definition 2.1(Event and state stopping). In theevent-stopped interface, a post-report kernel
emits (s′,e )∈S×{0, 1}. The valuee = 1 is permitted only after a productive call and commits
exactly once: the experiment stops, the labels′is retained, and the decoder returnsr(s′). No next
command is executed. The commitment event belongs to the public stopped transcript; it is not
an extra stored bit available during subsequent computation. On branches withe = 0, execution
continues ats′. A label may therefore be used both live and terminal on different branches.

4 QIAN QI
In thestate-stopped interface there is instead a fixed maph∗:S→{0, 1}. The initial label has
type zero. A transition commits if and only ifh∗(s′) = 1, and entry into type one is permitted
only after a productive report. Type-one labels are globally terminal and absorbing: they have no
executed command row. Type-zero labels are live. The halt status is thus completely determined
by the retained state, and live and terminal labels are disjoint.
Let Lγbe the set of labels reached before physical calls andTγthe set reached on commitment,
under the relevant family of path laws. The program’s role counts areℓγ=|Lγ|and tγ=|Tγ|, with

overlap is excluded. This is the distinction used below, not an unmentioned memory convention.

Appendix B. Scope and boundary examples
The center of the paper is a general sufficient-class acquired-geometry theorem, not a classification
of all positive causal experiments. Its calibrated two-sided assertion uses an actual effort witness
and bounded task-row discrepancies from a separately prepared comparison, which need not be
an operating model. It does not assume that a competing program stops under the comparison
dynamics. The exact specialization uses a fixed admissible witness with a common productive
task law and an all-strategy effort inequality, with a matched upper effort constant for exactness,
together with one common task-balancing program. It does not require a common primary row for
all models or all strategies. If two histories in the same alleged driver state have success probabilities
1/4 and 3/4, a single exact driver row cannot represent both. The present upper still works when a
proved conditional attempt bound and the task-measure balance remain valid; otherwise neither the
finite-driver formula nor the new theorem is licensed.
Pointwise calibration is not necessary for these minimax laws. Static hidden signs have zero
residual variance after fully revealing histories, and nearly pure quantum states can do the same.
Positive current-report marks then fail on those fibers. The raw reference-plus-balance argument
avoids that lower-variance premise; it does not assert that every such failed calibration can be
repaired. Conversely, report-only balance and an unaffordable reference preparation are insufficient,
as is a reference model whose supposedly unpredictable productive state is already leaked by a
preceding report.
Action aliasing is harmless only when it preserves physical ports, costs, observable inputs and
legal continuation kernels. Duplicating one physical command into two names does not increase
Proposition 10.4’s count. A phase-dependent dispatcher that can see an otherwise unavailable port
state is an extra resource, not a relabeling. The proposition is not a universal minimal-controller
characterization. Nor does a live lower exclude terminal reuse. Definition 2.1 and Lemma 10.5 keep
the two semantics separate; Proposition 18.2 charges any stateful translator before permitting role
identification.
The finite-state upper is an explicit recursion: at the two physical port labels, issue the declared
command; at the productive call, compute the virtual mark and finite decision; retain only the
next label. It has no history tape, accurate hidden posterior, free real register, free time counter
or externally randomized persistent program. Exact Borel descriptions and finite bit descriptions
are distinguished by Proposition 17.2. Optimal joint program/time/workspace complexity remains
unproved.
The two intervention realizations score the post-command audit. The Gaussian theorems preserve
the original current sign or direction and use no intervention on it. The directional theorem
combines a fresh-reference variance lower with a static-direction output-covering lower; it does not
add separately witnessed lower losses as if one model realized both. These are different declared
tasks and are never exchanged by an untyped reduction. The reference-law geometry is derived from
actual preparation and its cost is included, but its existence remains an experiment-class assumption.
General learning of an unknown gate lower bound, unrestricted kernel learning, arbitrary unbounded
losses, nonterminating protocols, infinite-dimensional unbounded operators, and large-deviation
equivalence are not conclusions of the paper. The stopped results proved here use nonnegative costs
